data.title: Companies Like Upland Resources (LON:UPL) Can Afford To Invest In Growth
data.description:
Just because a business does not make any money, does not mean that the stock will go down. For example, biotech and mining exploration companies often lose money for years before finding success with a new treatment or mineral discovery. But while the successes are well known, investors should not ignore the very many unprofitable companies that simply burn through all their cash and collapse.

So, the natural question for Upland Resources (LON:UPL) shareholders is whether they should be concerned by its rate of cash burn. In this report, we will consider the company's annual negative free cash flow, henceforth referring to it as the 'cash burn'. The first step is to compare its cash burn with its cash reserves, to give us its 'cash runway'.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Does Upland Resources Have A Long Cash Runway?

A cash runway is defined as the length of time it would take a company to run out of money if it kept spending at its current rate of cash burn. In June 2026, Upland Resources had UK£2.7m in cash, and was debt-free. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through UK£674k. Therefore, from June 2026 it had 4.0 years of cash runway. A runway of this length affords the company the time and space it needs to develop the business. Depicted below, you can see how its cash holdings have changed over time.

View our latest analysis for Upland Resources

How Is Upland Resources' Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

Because Upland Resources isn't currently generating revenue, we consider it an early-stage business. Nonetheless, we can still examine its cash burn trajectory as part of our assessment of its cash burn situation. From a cash flow perspective, it's great to see the company's cash burn dropped by 86% over the last year. While that hardly points to growth potential, it does at least suggest the company is trying to survive. Upland Resources makes us a little nervous due to its lack of substantial operating revenue. We prefer most of the stocks on this list of stocks that analysts expect to grow.

How Easily Can Upland Resources Raise Cash?

There's no doubt Upland Resources' rapidly reducing cash burn brings comfort, but even if it's only hypothetical, it's always worth asking how easily it could raise more money to fund further growth. Generally speaking, a listed business can raise new cash through issuing shares or taking on debt. One of the main advantages held by publicly listed companies is that they can sell shares to investors to raise cash and fund growth. By looking at a company's cash burn relative to its market capitalisation, we gain insight on how much shareholders would be diluted if the company needed to raise enough cash to cover another year's cash burn.

Upland Resources' cash burn of UK£674k is about 1.5% of its UK£45m market capitalisation. That means it could easily issue a few shares to fund more growth, and might well be in a position to borrow cheaply.

So, Should We Worry About Upland Resources' Cash Burn?

As you can probably tell by now, we're not too worried about Upland Resources' cash burn. In particular, we think its cash burn reduction stands out as evidence that the company is well on top of its spending. And even its cash burn relative to its market cap was very encouraging. After taking into account the various metrics mentioned in this report, we're pretty comfortable with how the company is spending its cash, as it seems on track to meet its needs over the medium term. On another note, Upland Resources has 3 warning signs (and 2 which are concerning) we think you should know about.

data.title: We Think U10's (EPA:ALU10) Solid Earnings Are Understated
data.description:
U10 Corp (EPA:ALU10) announced a healthy earnings result recently, and the market rewarded it with a strong uplift in the stock price. Looking deeper at the numbers, we found several encouraging factors beyond the headline profit numbers.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Zooming In On U10's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

U10 has an accrual ratio of -0.21 for the year to June 2026. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of €14m, well over the €2.40m it reported in profit. Notably, U10 had negative free cash flow last year, so the €14m it produced this year was a welcome improvement.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On U10's Profit Performance

Happily for shareholders, U10 produced plenty of free cash flow to back up its statutory profit numbers. Because of this, we think U10's underlying earnings potential is as good as, or possibly even better, than the statutory profit makes it seem! And it's also positive that the company showed enough improvement to book a profit this year, after losing money last year. Of course, we've only just scratched the surface when it comes to analysing its earnings; one could also consider margins, forecast growth, and return on investment, among other factors. KE Holdings (BEKE) drew fresh attention after the share price moved 5.5% higher on strong trading volume, as investors focused on a leaner cost base and a higher-margin business mix.

Interest also centers on improving demand for existing-home transactions and expectations for quarterly earnings of US$0.25 per share, which would indicate higher profitability compared with the same period a year earlier.

At around US$18.85, KE Holdings has put together a clear upswing, with a 30 day share price return of 11.41% and a year to date share price gain of 17.37%. The 1 year total shareholder return of 22.66% hints that investors are warming to the leaner cost base and higher margin mix over a longer stretch, even as sentiment still reflects the risks embedded in its 5 year total shareholder return, which is down 11.12%.

After a sharp rebound and a cleaner cost structure, KE Holdings now sits at an interesting fork in the road. Has most of the easy upside already played out, or does valuation still leave meaningful room ahead?

Most Popular Narrative: 21% Undervalued

On Simply Wall St's most followed narrative, KE Holdings is assessed with a fair value of $23.92 against the recent $18.85 close, which frames the current rebound as still leaving a valuation gap on the table.

The main factor that has to go right is that KE Holdings continues to shift its business mix toward existing home transactions, higher margin renovation and rental services, and AI-supported productivity, while maintaining cost discipline.

The numbers on profits, cash of about RMB 65.6b to RMB 67.3b and sizeable buybacks that have retired roughly 14.8% of prior shares imply a market valuation that still prices KE Holdings as if these efficiency and capital return gains are only partly reflected in the share price.

Still, the KE Holdings story can be knocked off course if China’s housing weakness continues or if renovation and rental expansion runs into deeper demand issues.

Another View: KE Holdings Through The P/E Lens

Our DCF work points to KE Holdings trading below an estimate of its future cash flow value, yet the plain P/E picture looks much tighter. The stock changes hands at 30.5x earnings compared with a 14.2x P/E for the wider US Real Estate group, a sizeable premium that leans on stronger growth and quality perceptions.

Against closer peers on 42.6x, BEKE screens cheaper, but relative to a fair ratio of 29.5x, the current multiple still sits slightly rich. That mix of discount versus peers, premium versus the sector and only a small gap to the fair ratio raises a blunt question: Is this more a quality story with limited valuation cushion, or an entry point that still rewards patience if the thesis holds?

data.title: How Strong Earnings Results At CCB Changed Its Investment Story
data.description:
• China Construction Bank reported third quarter 2026 net interest income of CNY 160,888 million and net income of CNY 104,662 million, with nine month earnings also above the prior year and basic EPS from continuing operations at CNY 0.38 for the quarter and CNY 1.03 for the period.
  • The bank paired this earnings update with a RMB 2.142b preferred dividend plan and the nomination of economist Cai Hongbin as an independent non executive director, which together highlight both capital distribution decisions and board level expertise on credit, regulation and long term policy trends.
  • Attention now turns to how China Construction Bank's net interest income profile might reshape the investment narrative that analysts previously outlined.
Spot opportunities across the wider bank sector by scanning our curated 212 resilient stocks with low risk scores, which reflects China Construction Bank's focus on earnings resilience and disciplined capital return.

China Construction Bank Investment Narrative Recap

To own China Construction Bank, you need to be comfortable with a large, system level lender that leans heavily on net interest income and policy priority sectors such as technology, green and inclusive finance. The latest quarterly figures show this interest engine still working, which matters for supporting dividends and absorbing credit swings.

The short term swing factor is whether margins and asset quality hold as loan books tilt toward these focus areas and cross border activity. Key risk sits with renewed pressure on loan yields or regulatory limits that squeeze NIM or fee pools. The recent updates do not radically change that equation.

The most relevant piece of recent news for that equation is the preferred share dividend plan on the RMB 60b domestic issuance. A fixed 3.57% coupon and RMB 2.142b payout signal how China Construction Bank continues to manage funding costs while servicing hybrid capital alongside common equity distributions.

For you as a shareholder, the way this preferred layer is serviced interacts with the core catalyst in earnings resilience. Stronger net interest income and fee lines need to comfortably fund both these contractual payouts and ordinary dividends. If margins compress or non interest revenue weakens, this additional capital stack could limit flexibility.

China Construction Bank's analyst narrative points to CN¥954.5b in revenue and CN¥405.7b in earnings by 2029, anchored on expected revenue growth of 15.1% a year and an earnings increase of about CN¥65.5b from CN¥340.2b today.

Some bullish analysts see the board change itself as a catalyst. They already pencilled in revenue of about CNY 1,134.1b and earnings of CNY 424.8b by 2029 for China Construction Bank, far above the lower CNY 954.5b consensus revenue view. Investors can treat this fresh appointment and dividend plan as reasons to revisit both narratives.

data.title: Cambi ASA (OB:CAMBI) Just Reported And Analysts Have Been Lifting Their Price Targets
data.description:
Shareholders might have noticed that Cambi ASA (OB:CAMBI) filed its second-quarter result this time last week. The early response was not positive, with shares down 3.0% to kr22.60 in the past week. Overall the results were a little better than the analysts were expecting, with revenues beating forecasts by 8.1%to hit kr265m. This is an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance in its report, look at what experts are forecasting for next year, and see if there has been any change to expectations for the business. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Cambi's two analysts is for revenues of kr1.03b in 2026. This reflects a reasonable 7.3% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of kr1.03b and earnings per share (EPS) of kr0.70 in 2026. So we can see that while the consensus made no real change to its revenue estimates, it also no longer provides an earnings per share estimate. This suggests that revenues are what the market is focusing on after the latest results.

Check out our latest analysis for Cambi

The average price target rose 27% to kr28.00, with the analysts clearly having become more optimistic about Cambi'sprospects following these results.

Another way we can view these estimates is in the context of the bigger picture, such as how the forecasts stack up against past performance, and whether forecasts are more or less bullish relative to other companies in the industry. It's pretty clear that there is an expectation that Cambi's revenue growth will slow down substantially, with revenues to the end of 2026 expected to display 15% growth on an annualised basis. This is compared to a historical growth rate of 19% over the past five years. Juxtapose this against the other companies in the industry with analyst coverage, which are forecast to grow their revenues (in aggregate) 11% per year. So it's pretty clear that, while Cambi's revenue growth is expected to slow, it's still expected to grow faster than the industry itself.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that the analysts reconfirmed their revenue estimates for next year, suggesting that the business is performing in line with expectations. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. There was also a nice increase in the price target, with the analysts clearly feeling that the intrinsic value of the business is improving.

We have estimates for Cambi from its two analysts out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here.

That said, it's still necessary to consider the ever-present spectre of investment risk. We've identified 1 warning sign with Cambi , and understanding it should be part of your investment process.
